newsitem.title: JAPAN: KDD says Japan Telecom tie-up one of many options.
newsitem.headline: KDD says Japan Telecom tie-up one of many options.

text.p: There is a possibility that Kokusai Denshin Denwa Co Ltd (KDD) will in the future tie up with the Japan Telecom Co Ltd group, but that is only one of many options, KDD president Tadashi Nishimoto said on Thursday.

Nishimoto also told a news conference he believed a delay in the granting of a U.S. licence to KDD for international operations was due to U.S.-Japan trade friction, particularly their differences over a 20 percent limit on foreign ownership in KDD.
"We thought it was appropriate for KDD to apply to apply for the licence through a simplified application procedure because KDD is already operating in the United States," Nishimoto said.
"We are only asking for an expansion of the service."
Nishimoto said KDD would consider what steps to take after reading a formal letter from the U.S. Federal Communications Commission (FCC).

KDD said on Wednesday that the U.S. Trade Representative's office, the Commerce Department and the State Department had asked that it be excluded from a simplified and speedy application procedure for a U.S. licence for international phone services.
Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT) also said its application had been similarly delayed.

Regarding a possible tie-up with a domestic telecom group, Nishimoto said: "There is a possibility of tying up with Japan Telecom and the ITJ group, but that is only one possibility and there are many options."

Japan Telecom, a long-distance domestic carrier, said on Wednesday that it and International Telecom Japan Inc (ITJ), one of Japan's smaller overseas carriers, were negotiating a possible merger and aimed to reach agreement by the end of March.
